podcast.title: Distribution Deal with EMI
podcast.body: Cargo Records, the indie label for the San Diego Blink, had an opportunity to sign a distribution deal with EMI to distribute the Irish Blink's records in North America, which further complicated the naming conflict. "And then Cargo Records, the San Diego Blinks indie label, had a chance to sign a distribution deal with EMI to distribute the Irish Blinks records in North America."

podcast.title: Major Deal and UK Attention
podcast.body: The Irish band secured a major record deal and began to gain significant attention in the United Kingdom throughout 1993 and 1994. "They ended up with a major deal and started getting attention in the UK through 1993 and 1994."

podcast.title: Prior Claim to Name "Blink"
podcast.body: An Irish band, previously known as Red and Dino, recorded new music under the name "Blink" in June 1991, predating the San Diego band's usage by several months. They also had music available for sale earlier, establishing their claim to the name. "Back in June of 1991, an Irish band, who used to go with the name Red and Dino, recorded some new tracks under the name Blink."
